adt.Node.description:
A Node can only refer to Nodes that already exist and cannot change after
construction, so a Node and everything it reaches form a finite acyclic
graph. Copying a Node shares it in constant time. Each Node stores its
height, the longest path to a leaf, and is released in a loop, so values of
any depth can be built and dropped.

algebra.Applicative.description:
The private `_Joined[L, R]`, `_join_left` and `_join_right` represent either
of two computations with the same payload. Eager families share one carrier
type; deferred families override the join to retain the selected computation.
Transformers and conditional recovery share this boundary without needing bind.
`_JoinCompatible[L, R]` describes construction admission for that choice;
deferred execution still validates its actual environment or state at run.

`collect` gathers every payload a callback produces over a source into a
`List`, and list traversal into this family uses it. It is the private
`_loop` with an append rule: one pull loop whose accumulation rule decides
how payloads combine and when the accumulator stops being live. The default
`_loop` runs over `pure`, `map` and `map2_lazy` and stops pulling once the
accumulator has failed. It requires an accumulator type that stays the same
across steps; a family whose combination changes type overrides the private
`_Looped`, `_LoopError` and `_loop` with its own single loop.

Left skips the callback. `pure` creates Right. `map2_lazy` skips its right
thunk on Left, otherwise forces it once and calls the combiner only when
both values exist. `flat_map` follows the same sequencing rule. Diagnostics
combine left to right with S, after the value callback, only when both
operands have diagnostics. `collect` uses the shared pull loop, stopping
after the first Left and retaining all preceding warnings. Empty input is
Right of an empty native List.

Carriers and library callbacks are consumed, including skipped owners.
Values and diagnostics need not be copyable. Native callback or policy
errors propagate immediately with their exact types and clean up all owned
values. Raising components must share one error type or raise Never.
Operations add constant tag work and no heap storage; collect adds its
output List and uses constant native stack space. Functor, Applicative and
Monad laws assume associative S and pure, terminating callbacks.

algebra.IorValidationFamily.description:
This alternative Applicative shares IorFamily's map, pure and combination
kernel. It forces the right thunk once even after Left. It keeps a combined
value only when both operands have values, and combines every present
diagnostic in left-to-right order. A value combiner runs before S.combine,
only when both values exist. Native raises stop immediately, including
raises from the diagnostic policy; they never become stored diagnostics.

List traversal and collect visit every input after stored Left values,
discarding partial successes while retaining warnings and errors together.
Empty input produces Right of an empty List. This policy is Applicative
only: it has no dependent flat_map. No threads or runtime wrapper are added.
Ownership, costs and error compatibility follow IorFamily. Applicative laws
assume associative S and pure, terminating callbacks.

overloads.description:
Native functions and closures are accepted directly and borrowed. A library
repeatable borrowing callback is consumed; shared partial predicates may instead be borrowed
by name. Built-in families run now, call once per payload
in native order, move accepted values unchanged and destroy rejected values.
Empty carriers skip calls. Failure destroys remaining input and partial output.

retain the native callback borrow. Keep it alive and unmoved until completion.
Generic forwarding of a raising native callback names its error with E=.

Another overload takes a native function or closure directly, for every

equal the carrier's element type, origins included. Generic code that
forwards a raising native callback names its error with `X=`.

instance: `map[OptionalFamily](twice, value^)`. It is borrowed, not moved:
an eager instance calls it before returning, and a deferred computation
keeps the borrow until it runs, so keep the callback alive and unmoved

equal the carrier's element type, origins included. Generic code that
forwards a raising native callback names its error with `X=`.

supplies the next state; Break supplies the result. Failure or absence
stops that branch. The family retains its branching order and deferred
execution; a branching family may require copies and grow its result set.

to the existing effectful fold and its native while loop. Custom families
must provide a stack-safe dependent fold to satisfy the same guarantee.

callables.BinarySignature.description:
`BinarySignature[A, B, R].capture(closure)` infers the closure's concrete
type and returns a `NativeBinary`. Supply `E` for a raising callback.
The default `Never` accepts both pure and explicitly `raises Never`
signatures. Use `type_of(None)` for a procedure with no return value;
an explicit `NoneType` result remains distinct.

Signature selection precedes callback admission, so rejected conventions
do not require inference of the input, result or error types from the
callback. No callback runs during capture. Ownership, copyability and
embedded origins remain those of the stored callable.

callables.BorrowSignature.description:
`BorrowSignature[A, R].capture(callback)` returns a `NativeBorrow` that
borrows `A` on each invocation and returns `R`. Supply `E` for a raising
callback. Plain functions, capturing closures and stored thin pointers are
accepted. Construction never calls the callback or copies its captures.

Input, result and error selection precede callback admission, so invalid
conventions do not require signature inference from an incompatible native
callback. `type_of(None)` denotes no return value; `NoneType` remains an
explicit result type. Both pure and explicitly `raises Never` callbacks
can use the default `E = Never`.

Construction pulls nothing. Each next call tests candidates once in source
order until the predicate returns False. Retained values move unchanged;
discarded values are destroyed. Exhaustion is fused, and abandoning the
iterator destroys owned source and callback state without further calls.
Callbacks cannot raise. Borrowed captures and source origins must remain
alive and unmoved while used; move an owned closure in with callback^.

overloads.description:
The step receives `(carry, element)` and returns `(next_carry, output)`;
the carry and output may have different types, and neither is copied. The
initial carry is not emitted (`fp.iteration.scan_left` emits snapshots
instead). Empty input returns the initial carry and an empty list. An
iterator input is collected into a `List` first, so it must be finite, and
every pull finishes before the first step. With no input, give `length` or
`static_length`; the step then receives `Tuple[]`. In reverse, running sums
over `[1, 2, 3]` give the carry `6` and the outputs `[6, 5, 3]`. On failure
the partial outputs, unused inputs and carry are destroyed.

data.Capture.description:
`Capture[E].mutable(state).take(value^).run(callback)` fixes the error type,
argument types and ownership before callback inference. Use `borrow` for
shared access, `mutable` for exclusive access, and `take` for consumption.
Up to three mixed positional operands can be followed by `kwargs`. `args` binds
zero to eight consumed operands, or extend an owned bundle with `take`. The bundle is movable and runs once.
An unused bundle destroys its owned arguments without calling anything.

Construct `Capture[E]()` before direct `run` or `stateful` admission.
This fixes E before a native callback is matched. A reusable context such
as `var capture = Capture[E]()` also provides `capture.args(...)`,
`capture.borrow(...)`, `capture.mutable(...)`, `capture.take(...)` and
`capture.kwargs(...)`; it stores no arguments and is reusable after errors.

Pure functions produce `Result[R, Never]`; raising functions retain E.
No-value callbacks return `Result[None, E]`. Native callbacks are borrowed
for the call; library thunk owners are consumed and retain their own error.
Thunks use consuming, mutable, then shared receiver priority. Pass
`mut_ref(thunk)` to retain a reusable owner and its updated state.
Empty keyword packs require K or a typed dictionary. `stateful` owns an
explicit state value for repeated calls through a plain native function.
Its owner is a mutable unary callable returning Result without raising.
Pass mut_ref(owner) to map or traverse while retaining its state, or move
owner into the operation. Mapping keeps outcomes; traversal stops on Err.
Existing `attempt` entry points remain available for compatibility.

data.Result.description:
`Ok` and `Err` convert to a `Result` wherever its type is known, as in
`return Ok(value)`; a payload must already have the exact type. `fp.match`
matches a `Result` with clauses for `Ok[T]` and `Err[E]`, which borrow the
stored constructor. It is `Copyable` only when both payloads are, and adds
constant tag work and no heap storage.

The transformations (`map`, `flat_map`, `map_err`, `or_else`) consume the
Result, so they chain: `parse(text).map(twice).flat_map(check)`. A callback
never runs on the inactive case, which passes through unchanged. A native
error a callback raises stays a native error: it never becomes the stored
`Err`, even when the types coincide. Callbacks are plain functions,
closures, or library values (`Unary` for the transformations and
`fold_owned`, `BorrowCallable` for `fold`, and the consuming forms of
`fold_once` and `fold_owned_once`). A generic wrapper names a raising
callback's error with `X=`, as in `value^.map[X=X](callback)`.

`flat_tap` and `flat_pair_with` borrow the success payload for a Result
projection, then move the original into the successful output. `followed_by`
and `before` take zero-argument Result factories, skipped on Err. `ensure`
borrows an Ok payload for a predicate and, only on rejection, an error
factory. `recover` consumes an error to produce an Ok of the same success
type, retaining the declared error type. `tap_err` borrows an Err payload
for inspection. These operations require no payload copies and run eagerly.
Owned library callbacks are consumed, including skipped callback owners;
named shared forms and native callbacks are borrowed in place.

have the same complete error type, including borrowed origins. Map
different error types explicitly before flattening. This is bind with

get_or_else.description:
Like Cats Either's `getOrElse`, evaluation of the default is lazy.
Mojo expresses that explicitly with a factory: it runs only on Err.
The Result and an owned library factory are consumed, including
destruction of a skipped factory. Named shared factories and native
factories are borrowed in place; a move or temporary retains ownership.
Plain functions infer their native error. For a captured factory raising
a custom error, use `pipeline(result^).raising[X]().get_or_else(factory)`.
Non-raising, Never and Error closures work directly. Library factories
retain their declared error without an extra context.

recover_if.description: Only Err runs the borrowing predicate. On True, the recovery consumes the error and returns the success type. On False, the original error remains. The stored error type stays unchanged. Native errors propagate unchanged; they never become stored Err values. Native callbacks are borrowed in place; library callbacks are consumed and use their declared receiver mode. Shared partial predicates and observers may instead be borrowed by name; an explicit move retains the owning form. Shared callable chains may instead be borrowed by passing their name; an explicit move retains the consuming form.

returns.doc: Recover a matching stored error as a success.

redeem.description: Both handlers return the same value type. The selected result is wrapped in Ok, retaining the original stored error type. Execution is immediate. Native handlers are borrowed in place; library handlers are consumed and use their declared receiver mode, including disposal of the skipped handler. Payloads, captures and native raised errors keep their ownership and origins. No Copyable requirement is added. Named shared callable chains are borrowed; move either handler explicitly to transfer its captures.

overloads.description:
Overloads take zero, one or two positional arguments with their native read,
`var` or `mut` conventions. Use `attempt_kwargs` for a callback with a
native keyword pack, including an empty pack. Pass consumed arguments
with `^`. Changes made through a `mut`
argument before a failure remain visible. Every declared positional
parameter must be supplied, including defaulted ones; other call shapes
are written as a closure passed to the zero-argument form.

On Mojo 1.2, an optional named convention selector avoids incompatible
overload inference: `attempt[owned=True](function, value^)` or
`attempt[owned_mut=True](function, value^, state)`. Unary selectors are
`read`, `owned` and `mutable`; binary names combine `read`, `owned`
and `mut` in argument order. A default scalar uses the owned family.
Selectors must be True and leave existing positional type bindings
unchanged. The borrowed `mutating`, `consuming` and `mut_owned`
adapters remain supported. For a diagnostic on an incompatible
selector, also bind `F=type_of(function)`; without this hint, Mojo 1.2
can crash before rejecting the callback.

The function is borrowed and reusable. A returned `Result` is ordinary
success data, and a declared `StopIteration` is captured like any other
error; process aborts are never caught.

overloads.description:
The callback must declare `var **kwargs: K`, optionally after zero, one
or two positional parameters with read, `var` or `mut` conventions. Pass
the callback and its positional arguments positionally, and pass consumed
arguments with `^`. Keyword values are homogeneous and owned; a
`StringDict[K]` can be expanded with `**options^`. An empty pack still uses
`attempt_kwargs(function)`. Optional named convention selectors match
`attempt` and describe only the positional prefix, for example
`attempt_kwargs[mutable=True](function, state, key=value)`. Use
`zero=True` for no positional prefix. Selectors must be True. The
`mut_owned_kwargs` adapter remains supported. For an incompatible
selector diagnostic, also bind `F=type_of(function)`.

The callback is borrowed and reusable. Mutation before failure remains
visible; its exact declared error, including `StopIteration`, is stored
as `Err`. A returned Result is ordinary success data. Every positional
parameter must be supplied, including defaulted ones. Named parameters
without a native keyword pack require a closure passed to `attempt`.

overloads.description:
`call_once` selects its consuming receiver, then mutable, then shared.
Receiver state, results and errors may be move-only; owned state is
destroyed on every path. Pass `mut_ref(thunk)` to retain the original
state for reuse or inspection, including after a captured failure.
References in the result or error must belong to owners that outlive the
consumed thunk.

A capability is a compile-time dictionary, not a runtime carrier. Generic
programs use `Family` for ordinary algebra operations. `ask` copies the
environment; forward `AskAvailable` in generic function constraints.
Implementations must return a Family carrier whose payload is Environment.

effects.Fiber.description:
Construct with unsafe_start. Dropping requests cancellation and waits for
the worker and its finalizers; this can block indefinitely in native code
which does not cooperate. Join explicitly to observe errors. The concrete
program type preserves captured origins and move-only values.

join_io.description:
Dropping this unopened recipe still drops and joins the owned fiber.
Child errors survive parent cancellation, with the canceled flag set.

effects.IOResource.description:
Default acquisition is masked until release is registered. Use is run in
the enclosing cancellation state, and release is masked. Product and bind
acquire left to right and finalize inside out, preserving every exact error.
Dropping an unopened recipe destroys captures without executing effects.

effects.ReaderT.description:
Every operation returns a concrete computation that stores its inputs; a
composed computation's type is the tree of its operations, and nothing runs
until `run`. Constructing a computation does not raise; its run raises the
exact common error of the stages it executes. On Mojo 1.1 that error cannot
propagate from a function declared with a plain `raises`; handle it with
`try`/`except`, where it keeps its exact type. The base is used only through
its Monad methods and, for recovery, its optional ApplicativeError capability.
Any Monad, including another Reader or State, can be
the base. Traversal delegates to the base's `collect`, whose callback runs
each produced computation with the borrowed environment.

effects.StateT.description:
Computations are built as for `ReaderT` and run with `run`. Traversal is one
loop: it checks that the base carrier still has a live branch, pulls one
item, calls the producer once, and binds the prepared computation across
the live branches, each on its own state. A failed, absent or empty carrier
stops producer calls and source pulls. The base carrier's type must stay
the same across steps, as it does for Identity, Optional, Result and List;
a deferred base is a compile error there.

Stored-error recovery is available when M implements ApplicativeError
and S is Copyable. Ordinary State operations still accept move-only state.

several states of the same type. Reading copies the state; modification
consumes it and returns its replacement. Move-only state supports updates
without supporting get. Implementations preserve the ordinary state laws:
get leaves state unchanged, the last put wins, and modifications compose
in execution order. Native failures follow the selected family's semantics.

effects.async_runtime.Async.description:
Pipeline, tail_rec_m, traverse and attempt select it from an IO. Every
operation returns an unopened IO; callbacks run once, when the program
reaches them, and their errors become the IO's failure. Folds and loops
run on the IO run loop in constant native stack. Callbacks must own their
state: borrowed callback views are rejected, so pass a native function or
an owned callable.

effects.async_runtime.IO.description:
Building an IO runs nothing. A value runs once, when a host drives it;
repeated work builds a fresh IO. Sequencing, recovery, and finalizers run
iteratively in constant native stack, and an unopened IO may be dropped.
Callbacks stored in an IO must own their state: plain functions and owned

effects.async_runtime.Instant.description:
Compare points only within a shared clock origin. Add checked Duration
values with after or the addition operator. The private two-word counter
permits ordinary timer arithmetic across Int.MAX and the low-word boundary;
it does not expose arbitrary numeric construction or a wall-clock timestamp.
Counter exhaustion, like wake-generation exhaustion, ends the runtime's
finite operational lifetime; ordinary bounded configuration cannot approach
its 128-bit horizon in one operation.

effects.async_runtime.protocols.Signal.description:
Copies share a revision. A signal does not establish cross-thread callback
safety, device completion, or memory visibility for external work. External
adapters retain those obligations until they report a terminal outcome.

effects.async_runtime.protocols.Step.description:
A terminal outcome certifies that entered work and cleanup are finished or
that their ownership was transferred into the result. A machine is never
polled after its terminal step. Runtime settlement and mask markers are
internal; extensions construct ready or pending without manipulating them.

effects.async_runtime.protocols.Wait.description:

pending, return changed with that captured revision; registration rechecks
it. Notification is a readiness hint, not synchronization for external work.
Cancellation remains a wake source when the execution context allows it.

functions.Composition.description:
The first stage to run may take zero, one or two arguments (a `Thunk`,
`Unary` or `Binary`, including plain functions and closures promoted with
`as_unary`); every later stage takes the previous result. Calling the
composition runs each stage once, in order, and a raised error stops it.
It is itself a `Thunk`, `Unary` or `Binary` in each receiver mode that all
its stages support: shared (`call`, `__call__`), exclusive (`call_mut`) or
consuming (`call_once`). Nothing runs during construction. It is `Copyable`
when every stage is, and copying is explicit.

A named shared unary composition can be reused as a selected Pipeline or
Result callback without copying its stages. The operation borrows it through
the existing shared receiver view. Use an explicit move to transfer the
stages, including into deferred results. Mutable and consuming-only chains
retain their existing owned admission.
Shared binary chains can be reused by name in `zip_with`, `map_with_index`,
`scan_map` and `scan_left`, with the same retained callback lifetime.

then.description:
Nothing runs during construction. The appended stage receives the
current result. Its input must match that exact type, and its raised
error must be compatible with the chain. Shared, mutable and consuming
receiver modes follow all stages.
The existing stage tuple is extended without copying captures or
storing the old composition as a nested stage. Reverse compositions
also run the new stage last. Move a named chain with `chain^.then(...)`.

returns.doc: A composition with the same entry arguments and one more stage.

functions.Kleisli.description:
Chaining only stores callbacks. `then` sequences through the family's bind,
`map` transforms successful payloads, `compose` prepends an effectful stage,
and `contramap` prepends an ordinary input transformation. All consume the
previous chain and their callback; use an explicit copy to keep a chain.

Shared and mutable calls borrow the callbacks. A deferred result retains
that borrow until it finishes. `call_once` transfers the callbacks to the
result and implements the library's `OnceUnary` protocol. No callback or
payload is copied implicitly.

functions.MappedPair.description:
Returned by `fp.functions.first` and `fp.functions.second`. The callback
moves into the wrapper without being called or copied. Calls consume the
pair, apply the callback to its selected element, and return a new pair.
The other element needs no copy capability. Exact result and error types,
receiver requirements and embedded origins are preserved.

Named shared wrappers can be reused by borrow in supported unary operations.
Move the wrapper to transfer its callback. Mutable calls retain callback
state, and consuming calls transfer its captures to the selected invocation.

functions.Partial.description:
Call it with the remaining arguments, which are borrowed. Each call passes
the function a fresh copy of every bound argument, so the stored values are
never consumed or changed. With 0, 1 or 2 remaining arguments it is also a
`Thunk`, `Unary` or `Binary`, which library higher-order functions accept.
A named unary Partial can be reused as a Pipeline or Result callback without
copying its stored prefix for admission. Each invocation still supplies the
native function with fresh copies of the bound arguments. An explicit move
transfers the Partial, including into deferred computations. Unary partials
also implement `BorrowCallable`: predicates, observers and borrowed-payload
handlers call the same native function without consuming the payload.
Selected Pipeline operations can reuse these partials by name.
With two remaining arguments, a named partial can also be reused by
`zip_with`, `map_with_index`, `scan_map` and `scan_left`; both remaining native arguments are read.

functions.Piped.description:
Each `then` applies one stage immediately, as `pipe(value, f)` does, and
infers that stage's types from its own call, so a chain has no stage limit
and takes plain functions, closures and library `Unary` values alike. `get`
extracts the stored value. `map` preserves supported native containers and
maps their payloads immediately; `map[I]` uses an explicit Functor family,
including its evaluation and error semantics. `filter` and `filter_not`
preserve supported containers; `fold_left` consumes an iterable immediately. `get` does
not trigger evaluation. Use `iterated(source).map(f)` for lazy element mapping.

attempt_tap.description: The observer borrows the entire Result, runs once on either branch and returns Result[U, E]. Its Ok payload is discarded and the original Result is retained; its Err replaces the original outcome. Native raised errors remain raised. Native errors propagate unchanged; they never become stored Err values. Native callbacks are borrowed in place; library callbacks are consumed and use their declared receiver mode. Shared partial predicates and observers may instead be borrowed by name; an explicit move retains the owning form.

a repeatable observer and copyable retained outcomes. Single-use paths
admit move-only values. Native callbacks remain borrowed until execution.

filter.description:
Without an explicit family, List, Deque, LinkedList, Dict, StringDict
and Optional filter immediately and keep their concrete type. Dictionary
predicates borrow values; keys, insertion order and hasher are preserved.
Accepted payloads move unchanged, rejected payloads are destroyed, and
empty inputs skip the predicate. Native callbacks are borrowed; library
repeatable borrowing callbacks are consumed. Each predicate only borrows its input.

Custom containers implement Filterable and use `filter[I](predicate)`.
Deferred families retain their own evaluation and error semantics and may
retain a native callback's borrow. Array cannot shrink while keeping its
type; Result needs an explicit error for rejection. Neither has an
automatic filter. Use `iterated` for lazy iterable filtering.

filter_not.description:
Automatic calls support the same six containers as filter and run
immediately. Each candidate is borrowed once; retained values move
unchanged. Dictionaries test values and keep keys, order and hasher.
Native callbacks are borrowed; library BorrowCallable values move.
Empty inputs skip the predicate. Failure stops traversal and destroys
partial output and remaining input, preserving the predicate's error.

Custom containers use `filter_not[I](predicate)` with their Filterable
family, including its deferred evaluation and associated result/error
types. Keep a borrowed native callback alive and unmoved for as long
as a deferred result uses it. Generic raising forwarding names E=E.

flat_tap_err.description: The projection runs only on Err and must return Result[U, E]. Its Ok payload is discarded and the original error is retained; its Err replaces that error. Ok passes through unchanged. Native errors propagate unchanged; they never become stored Err values. Native callbacks are borrowed in place; library callbacks are consumed and use their declared receiver mode. Shared partial predicates and observers may instead be borrowed by name; an explicit move retains the owning form.

flat_tap_err.description:
Success skips the observer. Native callbacks are borrowed until execution;
owned library callbacks move into the computation. Branching requires a
repeatable observer. Native raised errors propagate with their exact types.
Observer successes restore the original error. Observer failures follow
combination: Result keeps the observer error, Validation accumulates it
before the original. Empty effects remain empty. The family determines
timing and copies needed for branching; payloads are discarded first.

borrowed; deferred families retain that borrow. Use `as_unary(f^)` to
transfer a callback into a deferred result. With no explicit family,
supported native containers map immediately and preserve their kind;
dictionaries map values, preserving keys, order and hasher.

Limitations:
    Generic native callback forwarding names the family explicitly,
    and a raising callback names its error with `E=`. Automatic mapping
    supports List, Array, Deque, LinkedList, Dict, StringDict, Optional
    and Result. Other carriers require an explicit family. Filtering
    also preserves containers that can represent rejection.

Shared partial predicates and observers may instead be borrowed by name; an explicit move retains the owning form.

recover_if.description: Only Err runs the borrowing predicate. On True, the recovery consumes the error and returns the success type. On False, the original error remains. The stored error type stays unchanged. Native errors propagate unchanged; they never become stored Err values. Native callbacks are borrowed in place; library callbacks are consumed and use their declared receiver mode. Shared partial predicates and observers may instead be borrowed by name; an explicit move retains the owning form.

Exactly one handler consumes each original outcome. A handler failure
passes onward without invoking the other handler. The selected stored
error type stays fixed. Native callbacks remain borrowed until execution;
library callbacks move into the computation. Branching requires repeatable
handlers. Unselected callbacks are disposed through the existing family.

Only the original branch selects a handler; a returned Err never invokes the other handler. Execution is immediate. Native handlers are borrowed in place; library handlers are consumed and use their declared receiver mode, including disposal of the skipped handler. Payloads, captures and native raised errors keep their ownership and origins. No Copyable requirement is added.

tap_err.description: The inspector runs only on Err. Its return value is discarded; the error is moved back unchanged. Ok passes through without inspection. Native errors propagate unchanged; they never become stored Err values. Native callbacks are borrowed in place; library callbacks are consumed and use their declared receiver mode. Shared partial predicates and observers may instead be borrowed by name; an explicit move retains the owning form.

Success skips the observer. Native callbacks are borrowed until execution;
owned library callbacks move into the computation. Branching requires a
repeatable observer. Native raised errors propagate with their exact types.
The observer's result is discarded, including a returned stored failure.
The original error is reintroduced with the family's fail constructor.

parameters.description: The type of the value the chain holds.
parameters.name: Value

functions.Piped.summary: A value in an eager chained pipeline, started by `piped(value)`.

functions.Pipeline.description:
Start with `pipeline(value)` for native carriers, declared effect recipes or a bare value, or
`pipeline[Family](value)` for an explicit Functor. Select a native error
once with `raising[E]()`. Pure callbacks keep Never; library callbacks
keep their declared errors. `get()` extracts the value. `run(environment)`
executes Reader, `run(state)` executes State, and `run()` unwraps Writer.
`run_io()` executes IO with its exact outcome and cancellation boundary.
`guarantee` and `on_cancel` attach deferred IO cleanup; `guarantee_case`
constructs cleanup from the exit case. These delegate to
the existing effect runners and finalization owner. Map, flat_map,
filter and filter_map delegate to the family's evaluation and ownership
rules, including deferred execution and retained callback borrows.

`local` scopes the selected environment. `listen` pairs a payload with its
log, and `censor` transforms that log. Each delegates to the selected
capability, preserving its output family and construction error.

`elements()` selects native List, Array, Deque, LinkedList or NonEmptyList
element operations without naming a family. It only moves the carrier and
preserves the selected native error. The chosen family's shape and
capabilities still apply: Array keeps its length; NonEmptyList filtering
produces List. Other whole-value pipelines keep their existing semantics.

`tap` borrows the whole value once now, including empty carriers and Err.
`tap_each` borrows each payload through the family's map; `pair_with`
retains each original beside its projection. Observer results are
discarded for both tap forms. `filter_not` retains payloads rejected by
a borrowing Bool predicate. These operations consume a library
BorrowCallable or borrow a native closure; stored thin pointers are
copied. Observation preserves the selected family and native error context.
Mapping rebinds RebindingFunctor; filtering follows FilteredFamily or MapFilteredFamily; NonEmptyList filtering
continues as List because it may discard every element.

`flat_tap` and `flat_pair_with` sequence borrowing effects through the
selected Monad, retaining originals or pairing them with each projection.
`before` sequences a factory and keeps originals; `followed_by` keeps its
produced payloads. The family owns skipping, branching and deferred timing.
Retained originals need Copyable only when successful effects duplicate them.

`then` consumes the whole value once. It selects the returned List,
Optional, Result or declared effect family, or Identity for other values; `then[Family]`
selects an explicit output family. Folds consume a native source and
select the accumulator's family by the same rule. Traversal selects its
target effect family. `traverse_tap[TargetFamily]` borrows each payload,
runs its effect and retains the original. `filter_effect[TargetFamily]`
retains originals whose borrowing effect returns True; the source must
also support FunctorFilter. Both preserve the target's short-circuiting,
accumulation, branching and deferred timing. Single-use library callbacks
work where traversal calls them at most once. Branching targets may require
copyable payloads. Combinations retain the current Applicative family.

`traverse_filter` and `sequence_filter` compact Optional payloads inside
the target effect using the source's FunctorFilter. `flat_traverse` and
`flat_sequence` flatten one source layer using its Monad. `traverse_void`
and `sequence_void` discard successful outputs from native sources;
Result traversal retains its source error layer inside the target.

Effectful queries consume a native source into a target Monad.
`all_effect`, `any_effect` and `find_effect` borrow each item;
`find_map_effect` and `fold_map_effect` consume it. Bind a fold accumulator
before its callback with `fold_effect[TargetFamily](initial).run(step)`.
The target controls stopping, branching and deferral. Monoid identity
construction happens immediately; callback and combination timing follows
the target. Array sources move through temporary List storage.

Pure reductions consume sources immediately. `find_map` stops at the
first present projection. `fold_map[Monoid]` and `combine_all[Monoid]`
combine in source order; `sum` and `sum_by` infer numeric types and SIMD
lanes. `min_by` and `max_by` borrow each item for its key, preserving the
first item on ties. Reduction results select their native family.

Mapping conveniences retain the selected family. `fill`, `replace`, `void`
and tuple pairing use its map; copied constants must be Copyable.
`compact` requires FunctorFilter, `flatten` requires Monad, and `ap`
applies stored library callables through Applicative combination.

`if_effect(on_true, on_false)` uses the selected Monad's Bool condition.
A failed or absent condition skips both factories. Native closures remain
borrowed; thin pointers and library factories are owned. Repeated sources
require repeatable factories. Deferred families retain their invocation
timing and can join distinct carrier representations with one payload type.

`par_map_n`, `par_product_n`, `par_traverse` and `par_sequence` use ordered
Validation accumulation for stored Result errors. Native raises stop
immediately. List-valued errors infer concatenation; an explicit Semigroup
selects another error policy. N-ary methods retain the selected source
family; accumulating traversal continues in the resulting Result family.

Result-specific methods delegate to Result and update ResultFamily when
the stored error type changes. Native raised errors remain raised;
use Capture to store them. Existing Piped and piped remain available.

functions.RedeemContract.description:
Forward Compatible and project Family, Out and Error in a generic wrapper of
Pipeline.redeem. One handler consumes the original selected outcome; its native
error is never sent to the other handler. ApplicativeError suffices for family
execution, including Validation. Intrinsic Result behavior remains available
under non-error families. Mapping rebinds the output family where supported.
ReceiverCompatible checks both handlers for a shared, mutable or consuming
receiver. InvocationCompatible adds that check for new wrapper boundaries,
while existing Compatible proofs and family invocation requirements remain.

functions.RedeemContract.summary: Admission and result metadata for selected value-returning outcome handling.

functions.RedeemWithContract.description:
Forward Compatible and project Family, Out and Error in a generic wrapper of
Pipeline.redeem_with. Canonical and intrinsic Result handlers may agree on a new
stored-error type. Other selected families require ApplicativeError and Monad,
retaining their own error layer and execution semantics. Returned failures and
native raises never invoke the opposite handler. ReceiverCompatible checks
both handlers; InvocationCompatible adds receiver availability to Compatible
for new wrapper boundaries without changing existing generic proofs.

functions.Split.description:
Returned by `split(left, right)`. This is an alias for ordinary composition of
`first` and `second`, so receiver capabilities, copying, errors and origins
follow those existing owners. The left callback runs before the right callback.
functions.Split.signature: comptime Split[F: UnaryContract & Movable & Deinitable, G: UnaryContract & Movable & Deinitable] = Composition[False, 1, MappedPair[F, G.Arg, True], MappedPair[G, F.Out, False]]

functions.Tupled.description:
`tupled(function)((first, second))` calls the binary function with the two
owned elements. Nothing runs during construction. Captures, input elements
and raised errors are transferred without copying; result origins remain
those of the underlying callback.

Shared, mutable and consuming calls retain the wrapped receiver's modes.
Named shared wrappers can be reused by borrow in supported unary callback
operations. An explicit move transfers the wrapper and its stored callback.

overloads.description:
`compose(h, g, f)(x)` is `h(g(f(x)))`: the last argument runs first and may
take zero, one or two arguments. Plain functions, library values and
promoted closures are accepted as in `flow`. A mismatched stage is reported
by its position in the run order and its argument position.

Limitations:
    At most eight plain functions per call. A pair may mix one plain
    function or stored thin pointer with one library callable directly.
    Longer mixed chains append with `.then(...)`, group pairs or promote
    unary native stages with `as_unary`; capturing unary closures also
    use `as_unary`.

overloads.summary: Return one stage unchanged, with all its capabilities.

args.description: The stages, moved into the composition.
args.name: functions

overloads.description:
`flow(f, g, h)(x)` is `h(g(f(x)))`. Two to eight plain functions are accepted
as they are; library values such as partials, compositions and flipped
functions, and closures promoted with `as_unary`, are accepted in any
number. The first stage may take zero, one or two arguments; every later
stage takes the previous result, or the call does not compile, with an
error that names the stage.

Two-stage compositions also accept one plain function or stored thin
pointer beside one library callable, in either position. The native stage
needs no adapter; the composition owns both stages without calling them.

Limitations:
    At most eight plain functions per call. Longer mixed chains append
    stages with `.then(...)`, group compositions or promote unary native
    stages with `as_unary`.
    Capturing unary closures use `as_unary` for stored composition.

returns.doc: A `Composition` that runs the stages left to right.

overloads.description:
`merge(f, g)(value)` copies the input once for `f` and moves the original
into `g`. Both callbacks must accept the same exact type, which must be
`Copyable`. Construction owns the callbacks without invoking or copying
them. Each call invokes the left callback first; if it raises, the right
callback is skipped and its unused input is released.

The result is an ordinary flat composition. Raising callbacks must share
one exact error type; non-raising callbacks can join either side. Shared,
mutable and consuming calls require both callbacks to support that receiver.
Capturing unary closures enter through `as_unary`. Native no-value output
remains `type_of(None)` in the result pair.

overloads.description:
`partial(f, a)(b, c)` calls `f(a, b, c)`. The overloads bind zero to eight
leading arguments, as in `partial(f, a, b)`. Construction copies each bound
argument once and never calls `f`; every call passes `f` fresh copies, and
the remaining arguments are borrowed. The result keeps `f`'s error type.

Limitations:
    `f` must be a plain function (no captures) whose remaining parameters
    are read, not owned or `mut`; bound values must be `Copyable`; and a
    `Partial` cannot be the target of another `partial`. Keyword binding,
    reordering and the other cases are written as a closure.

overloads.description:
Each stage runs once, in order, and receives the previous stage's result as
an owned value; tuples and `Result` values pass whole. Two to eight plain
functions are accepted as they are, `pipe(value, parse, check, render)`;
library values such as partials and compositions, and closures promoted
with `as_unary`, are accepted in any number. A stage whose input is not the
previous result is a compile error that names the stage. `pipe[E=Failure]`
states the common error, and `pipe[Results, E]` every result type.

An inferred two-stage call can mix a plain function or stored thin pointer
with a shared library stage directly, in either position. The library
stage is borrowed and remains reusable after the call.

Limitations:
    At most eight plain functions per call, because Mojo 1.1 cannot read a
    function's signature from a variadic pack: nest calls, group stages
    with `flow`, or chain them with `piped`. Longer mixed calls and explicit
    error/result bindings promote native stages with `as_unary`, as do
    capturing closures in mixed calls. Stages that raise
    different error types are mapped to one type first.
overloads.raises_doc:
The error type that every raising stage declares; a pipeline of pure
stages does not raise.

returns.doc: The last stage's result.

overloads.description:
`split(f, g)((a, b))` produces `(f(a), g(b))`. Construction owns both
callbacks without invoking or copying them. Each call moves the elements,
invokes the left callback first, then invokes the right callback. If the
left callback raises, the right callback is skipped. Raising callbacks must
share one exact error type; non-raising callbacks may join either side.

Shared, mutable and consuming calls are available when both callbacks
support that receiver. Capturing unary closures enter through `as_unary`.
Native no-value outputs remain `type_of(None)` elements in the result.

returns.doc: A composition from `Tuple[F.Arg, G.Arg]` to `Tuple[F.Out, G.Out]`.

map_accumulate.description:
The step consumes (carry, element) and returns (next carry, output).
The finite source is pulled once per step, in order; empty input returns the initial carry.
Neither the carry nor elements nor outputs need to be Copyable. Mutable library steps
take priority over shared invocation; consuming-only steps are rejected.
Failures stop immediately and retain their exact type, including StopIteration.
Capture native closures with BinarySignature; named standard binary adapters can be reused.
Aliased native pointers select Y explicitly, and E for typed errors.

partition.description:
Construction pulls nothing and each source item is classified once. Branches are move-only.
Unbounded queues retain every pending value; BoundedFail yields Result elements,
discards all queued values on overflow and gives each live branch one terminal Err.
Close a branch to release its queue without draining upstream. Access is sequential;
reentrant or overlapping access aborts before a second mutable state borrow.

unzip.description:
Construction pulls nothing and each source item is classified once. Branches are move-only.
Unbounded queues retain every pending value; BoundedFail yields Result elements,
discards all queued values on overflow and gives each live branch one terminal Err.
Close a branch to release its queue without draining upstream. Access is sequential;
reentrant or overlapping access aborts before a second mutable state borrow.

order until the predicate returns False. Retained values move unchanged;
discarded values are destroyed. Exhaustion is fused, and abandoning the
iterator destroys owned source and callback state without further calls.

Construction pulls nothing and each source item is classified once. Branches are move-only.
Unbounded queues retain every pending value; BoundedFail yields Result elements,
discards all queued values on overflow and gives each live branch one terminal Err.

reentrant or overlapping access aborts before a second mutable state borrow.

overloads.description:
Takes one to sixteen clauses. A clause is a plain function or a lambda without
captures; its parameter type says which values it applies to, and a `when`
clause may decline. The clauses are checked when the program compiles. The
subject is one of:

- a `Node[F]`: a clause takes a constructor of `F`, whose recursive fields are
  declared either as stored, `Node[F]`, or as the result type, in which case
  they arrive already matched; or it takes `Node[F]`, which accepts any
  constructor. A clause returns the result or `Next(node)`, to continue with a
  smaller value.
- a value stored in place, such as `Choice[F]` or `Result[T, E]`: a clause
  takes a constructor, or the whole type.
- an `Optional[T]`: a clause takes `T` for a present value, `NoneType` for an
  absent one, or `Optional[T]`.

overloads.description:
A clause takes a constructor of `F` and returns the new `Node[F]`; its
recursive fields declared as `Node[F]` arrive already rewritten. Every other
node is rebuilt from its rewritten children, and a node whose children did not
change is reused, so sharing is preserved. A `when` clause may decline. The
rewrite is a single pass.

parameters.description: The clause's result type: `Node[F]`, or a guarded `Node[F]`.
parameters.name: O0

parameters.description: The clause's error type, `Never` for a pure clause.
parameters.name: E0

overloads.raises_doc: The clauses' common error; a rewrite of pure clauses does not raise.

returns.doc: The rewritten value.

adt.description:
A data type lists its constructors, ordinary structs, in a `Cases`; a
constructor field that holds a value of the same type has the layer's
parameter `R`, `List[R]` or `Optional[R]`:

```text
struct Expr(Data):
    comptime Layer[R: Value] = Cases[Num, Add[R], If[R, R]]
```

A value holds one constructor, and comes in two kinds:

- `Node[F]` is immutable and shared: copying it shares it in constant time. A
  node can only refer to nodes that already exist, so a value is a finite
  acyclic graph. Recursive data needs it; each node is one allocation.
- `Choice[F]` is owned and stored in place, in a native `Variant`, with no
  allocation, for a type with no recursive field. Copying it copies the
  constructor.

A constructor converts to either implicitly. `fp.match` matches both, and
`fp.rewrite` transforms nodes.
adt.summary: Algebraic data types declared from your own structs, and their values.

algebra.description:
| Interface | Primitive operations | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Functor` | `map[I](f, value)` | Transform a payload without changing its context |
| `Filterable` | `filter[I](predicate, value)` | Retain accepted payloads without changing their types |
| `FunctorFilter` | `filter_map[I](transform, value)` | Transform payloads and retain present Optional results |
| `Applicative` | `pure[I](value)`, `map2_lazy[I](f, left, right)` | Introduce a payload; combine independent computations |
| `ErrorRecovery` | `I.or_else(handler, value)` | Recover the selected stored-error channel; terminal states may bypass it |
| `ApplicativeError` | `fail[I, A](error)`, `I.or_else(handler, value)` | Construct or recover the selected stored-error layer |
| `ErrorMapping` | `I.bimap[Target](on_ok, on_err, source)` | Transform success and one selected stored-error channel with an admitted destination policy |
| `Monad` | `flat_map[I](f, value)` | Choose the next computation from the current payload |
| `Traversable` | `traverse[S, G](f, source)` | Visit a source shape `S` in an applicative context `G` |
| `Semigroup` | `combine[S](left, right)` | An associative, ordered combination |
| `Monoid` | `empty[M]()`, `combine[M](left, right)` | An identity and an associative, ordered combination |

An instance is a compile-time dictionary named at each call: there are no
runtime interface objects and no global registry. The native instances are
`IdentityFamily` (the bare value), `OptionalFamily`, `ResultFamily[E]` and
`ListFamily`; `ValidationFamily[S]` uses Result storage with accumulating errors, with `StringMonoid` and `ListMonoid[A]`. `IorFamily[S]` sequences values with
warnings; `IorValidationFamily[S]` accumulates independent diagnostics. `fp.effects` adds
Reader, State, Writer and transformers. Each operation is a static method of
the instance and the functions here forward to it; its result and error types
are associated aliases of the instance, such as `I.Mapped[V, F]` and
`I.MapError[V, F]`, so generic code states them directly. The derived
operations `map2`, `ap`, `flatten` and `sequence` add no execution path.

Callbacks are fixed-arity values in any receiver mode: a `Unary` for `map`,
`flat_map` and `traverse`, a `Binary` combiner and a `Thunk` right operand for
`map2_lazy`. `map`, `flat_map` and `traverse` also take native functions and
closures directly. Operations consume carriers and callbacks. A callback that
runs repeatedly, as over a `List`, must have a shared or exclusive receiver; a
consuming-only callback is rejected when the program compiles. Native errors
propagate with their exact types; stored `Result` errors remain data.

`Filterable` is independent of Functor. ListFamily and OptionalFamily support
`filter` and its derived `filter_not`, with a repeatable borrowing predicate (`BorrowCallable` or `BorrowMutableCallable`) returning Bool. Owned predicates prefer their mutable receiver. Native
predicates are borrowed; owned library predicates are consumed. Selection runs
immediately and preserves the original payloads, origins and carrier type.

FunctorFilter extends Functor with filter_map. It may change payload types and
discard absent results; compact derives from it with identity. ListFamily and
OptionalFamily implement this capability. Custom Filterable families remain
independent and need no new methods.

A third-party instance implements the associated types and static methods of
the interfaces it claims, receives callbacks through their contracts and calls
them with `call_once` or `call_repeated` from `fp.callables`; it needs no
private library code. An Applicative-only target receives list traversal
through the default `collect`.

The functor, monad and monoid laws hold under pure, terminating callbacks and
equivalent native ownership behavior; callbacks with effects have a specified
call order and count instead.
algebra.summary: Functor, Filterable, FunctorFilter, Applicative, ApplicativeError, ErrorRecovery, ErrorMapping, Monad, Traversable, Semigroup and Monoid over native values, with explicit instances.

callables.description:
Every higher-order operation calls user code through these protocols. A
callable fixes its argument, result and error types in a contract trait, and
implements each receiver mode it supports as its own trait:

| Arity | Shared | Exclusive | Consuming |
|---|---|---|---|
| one owned argument | `Unary.call` | `MutableUnary.call_mut` | `OnceUnary.call_once` |
| two owned arguments | `Binary.call` | `MutableBinary.call_mut` | `OnceBinary.call_once` |
| no argument | `Thunk.call` | `MutableThunk.call_mut` | `OnceThunk.call_once` |
| one borrowed argument | `BorrowCallable.invoke` | `BorrowMutableCallable.invoke_mut` | `BorrowOnceCallable.invoke_once` |

`call_once` calls a callable of any mode once, preferring the consuming mode;
`call_repeated` calls one that stays usable, and requires `RepeatableUnary`,
`RepeatableBinary` or `RepeatableThunk`. `as_unary` moves a native function or
closure into a `NativeUnary`. Borrowing callables read their argument instead
of taking it. `invoke_borrowed`, `invoke_borrowed_repeated` and
`invoke_borrowed_once` provide shared, repeated exclusive and owned one-call
invocation. The latter accepts every receiver mode, preferring consuming,
then mutable, then shared.
`shared_ref(callback)` selects the shared receiver explicitly and keeps every
shared call shape. The copyable `SharedRef` lends a callback without copying
its captures and supplies a public reference type for generic contracts.
`mut_ref(callback)` lends a named library callback to an operation that owns
its callback, retaining the original state for inspection or reuse afterward.
The movable `MutableRef` preserves every repeatable shape and its native origin.
`CallContract` is the shared result/error metadata of owned-argument callables.
`RepeatableBorrow` admits shared or mutable borrowing receivers. Errors keep their exact types. `Partial`,
`Composition`, `Flipped`, `Tupled`, `MappedPair` and `Identity` from `fp.functions` implement these
protocols.

`as_binary` stores a plain binary function or thin pointer in `NativeBinary`.
It preserves two owned argument types and the exact result and error types.
Named adapters can be reused by shared borrow in `zip_with`, `map_with_index`,
`scan_map` and `scan_left`. The factory does not infer capturing closures.
`BinarySignature[A, B, R, E].capture(closure)` selects the signature before
capturing a binary closure into the same adapter. Its error defaults to `Never`.
`BorrowSignature[A, R, E].capture(callback)` stores a predicate, observer or
projection in `NativeBorrow`. Named uses share the adapter; each call reads
its payload. Native closures and thin pointer aliases retain their exact types.

Where each consumer enters:

| Consumer | Accepts |
|---|---|
| `pipe`, `flow`, `compose` | Two to eight plain functions, or library stages; inferred two-stage calls also mix a plain function or stored thin pointer with one library stage directly. `pipe` borrows a shared stage; compositions own their stages. Capturing unary closures use `as_unary`. |
| `piped(...).then` | Plain functions, closures and `Unary` values, one per call, with no limit |
| `flip` | `Binary` values and plain functions with two or more parameters |
| Lazy `map`, `filter_map`, `flat_map`, `scan_left` | Native callbacks and shared or mutable library unary/binary values |
| `fori_loop`, `while_loop`, `scan` | Native callbacks and shared-receiver `Unary`/`Binary` values |
| `fori_loop_mut` | A named shared or mutable library binary body, borrowed exclusively; updated receiver state remains in the caller. |
| Iterator filter, prefix, partition, search and count predicates | Native predicates, `BorrowCallable` and owned `BorrowMutableCallable` |
| Family `filter` and `filter_not` | Native predicates, shared views and owned `BorrowMutableCallable` or `BorrowCallable`; `mut_ref` preserves caller-owned state. |
| `while_loop` predicates | Native predicates and `BorrowCallable` |
| `Result` methods and folds | Native callbacks, `Unary`, `OnceUnary`, `BorrowCallable` and `BorrowOnceCallable` |
| `attempt_once` | `Thunk`, `MutableThunk` or `OnceThunk`; consuming, then mutable, then shared receiver priority |
| `fp.match` and `fp.rewrite` clauses | Plain functions and lambdas without captures, taking one to three parameters |
| `fp.algebra`, `fp.effects` | Native functions and closures for `map`, `flat_map`, `traverse`, `modify`, `censor` and `local`; `Unary`, `Binary`, `Thunk` in any receiver mode; `BorrowCallable` for Reader's `local` and `action`, which also takes `BorrowOnceCallable` |

Lazy iteration callbacks are non-raising, because the native iterator protocol
raises only `StopIteration`; terminal callbacks keep their own error channel.
callables.summary: How the library calls user code: callable protocols, receiver dispatch and native functions as values.

combinators.description:
Collection operations re-export fp.iteration; if_effect re-exports fp.algebra.
Sources are native iterators
at their current position, or owned iterables consumed into their iterators.
Transformations are lazy and require non-raising callbacks. Searches, folds,
sums and effectful traversal are terminals, preserving their exact errors.
Effectful reductions use a Monad target; if_effect selects a factory from an
effectful Bool. Reader and State targets defer execution until run.

Piped offers the same names with eager native container behavior; Iter offers
lazy transformations and immediate terminals. Mapping conveniences share element
adapters, and reductions share the accumulation driver. Native Piped dictionary
transformations and monoidal reductions use values; effectful folds and
predicates follow native iteration, as fold_left does; direct operations follow the source's native iteration.
Whole-value tap is available on Piped, including for ordinary structs.
combinators.summary: Direct combinators shared with fluent pipelines.

control.description:
They follow the sequential value semantics of JAX's control-flow operations,
without tensor stacking, tracing, autodiff or a JIT. Branch with Mojo's `if`.

The carry may be any value: a scalar, a SIMD value, a string, a container or a
move-only owner. Its type stays fixed, and nothing copies it. A callback is a
plain function or a closure, with separate pure and raising overloads, or a
shared-receiver library value: `Unary` for a `while_loop` body, `Binary` taking
`(Int, carry)` for a `fori_loop` body, and a `Binary` step for `scan`. A
scan infers its output type; `scan[Y](step, ...)` selects it explicitly.
Owned scan steps may also be `MutableBinary`, with mutable invocation preferred;
`mut_ref(step)` retains the original state. A `while_loop` predicate may
be a `BorrowCallable`. A call needing keywords or defaults is written as a
closure. Callbacks keep one receiver throughout.

Use `fori_loop_mut` to borrow a named library body exclusively and retain its
mutable state after the call. It accepts shared or mutable binary callbacks,
preferring mutable invocation when both are available. `fori_loop` also owns
moved or temporary repeatable bodies with that preference; `mut_ref(body)`
retains the original state. Named shared bodies keep their borrowed behavior.
Both forms share bounds, unrolling and errors.

Ordinary `while_loop(predicate, body^, carry)` owns a repeatable library body;
mutable invocation wins over shared. It accepts owned or borrowed predicates
through the same boundary. `mut_ref` retains either original receiver. Named
shared predicate/body pairs keep their borrowed shared calls.

`while_loop_mut(predicate, body, carry)` borrows a named unary body exclusively
with the same repeated receiver preference. It also owns shared or mutable
borrowing predicates; pass `mut_ref(predicate)` to retain their updated state.
Named shared `BorrowCallable` predicates, plain functions and stored thin
pointers keep their borrowed admission. Capturing predicates
and pointer aliases use `BorrowSignature[A, Bool, E].capture(callback)`.

Errors stop the loop at once. A predicate and a body must raise one error type,
including any embedded origins, or one of them nothing. Nothing retries or
rolls back effects.

The compile-time parameter `unroll` expands that many steps per rolled
iteration, with exact bounds checks for the final partial chunk; `1`, the
default, keeps a rolled loop. `unroll=0` fully expands a statically bounded
loop: `fori_loop[lower, upper, unroll=0](body, initial)` or
`scan[static_length=N, unroll=0](...)`. Full unrolling without static bounds,
a negative factor and an invalid static length are compile errors.
`while_loop` has no unroll parameter.
control.summary: Functional loops and scans over native Mojo values: `while_loop`, `while_loop_mut`, `fori_loop`, `fori_loop_mut` and `scan`.

data.description:
`Result[T, E]` holds a success value `Ok[T]` or a stored failure `Err[E]`.
`ok[E](value)` and `err[T](error)` infer the type of the payload they receive.
`ControlFlow[B, C]` holds `Break[B]` or `Continue[C]`. `Ior[E, A]` holds
`Left[E]`, `Right[A]` or `Both[E, A]` for values with diagnostics. These are stored in place
and matched by `fp.match`. Mojo's typed native errors are efficient; `Result`
is for failures that must be stored, collected or passed along as values, not
a replacement for `raises`.

The bridges: `attempt`, `attempt_kwargs` and `attempt_once` turn a raising call into a `Result`,
`raise_on_err` turns it back, each with the original error type, and
`collect_results` collects a source of Results into one.
data.summary: Typed results, early termination and bridges between raised and stored errors.

effects.description:
| Family | Value | Additional operations |
|---|---|---|
| `ReaderT[M, R]` | A `ReaderAction`: borrows `R` when run, returns `M`'s carrier | `action`, `run`, `lift`, `ask`, `asks`, `local` |
| `StateT[M, S]` | A `StateAction`: consumes `S` when run, returns `M`'s carrier of `(A, S)` | `action`, `run`, `run_value`, `run_state`, `lift`, `get`, `inspect`, `put`, `modify` |
| `WriterT[M, W]` | A `WriterValue` wrapping `M`'s carrier of `(W.Value, A)` | `writer`, `run`, `run_value`, `run_log`, `lift`, `tell`, `listen`, `censor` |
| `OptionalT[M]` | `M`'s carrier of `Optional[A]` | `lift` |
| `ResultT[M, E]` | `M`'s carrier of `Result[A, E]` | `lift` |

`Reader[R]`, `State[S]` and `Writer[W]` are the transformers over
`IdentityFamily`; `OptionalT` and `ResultT` over Identity are `OptionalFamily`
and `ResultFamily[E]` themselves. Each family is a `Monad` of `fp.algebra`, so
`map`, `pure`, `flat_map`, `map2_lazy` and `traverse` apply to its values.
Reader and State values are deferred computations: nothing runs until `run`.

Ask/Local and Stateful are compile-time capability dictionaries. Reader and
State select their own environment or state; LiftAsk, LiftLocal and
LiftStateful explicitly select a capability from the immediate base. Generic
programs use the selected dictionary's Family for algebra operations.
Tell/Listen/Censor select a log; LiftTell, LiftListen and LiftCensor transport
those operations through one layer. Listen pairs the payload with an observed
log, while censor transforms only the selected computation's output log.

Transformer order matters. `StateT` over `Result` returns no state on failure;
`ResultT` over `State` can return a failed `Result` together with the updated
state. Neither rolls back external mutation. For `ResultT[State[S], E]`, run
with `run[State[S]]`, whose result is `Tuple[Result[A, E], S]`, and lift
State's operations into the ResultT layer; for `StateT[ResultFamily[E], S]`,
run with that StateT, whose result is `Result[Tuple[A, S], E]`.

| Stack | Evaluation order | Final shape |
|---|---|---|
| `WriterT[Reader[R], W]` | Writer `run`, then Reader `run` | `(log, value)` |
| `ReaderT[Writer[W], R]` | Reader `run`, then Writer `run` | `(log, value)` |
| `WriterT[State[S], W]` | Writer `run`, then State `run` | `((log, value), state)` |
| `StateT[Writer[W], S]` | State `run`, then Writer `run` | `(log, (value, state))` |

`OptionalT[ResultT[M, E]]` carries `M[Result[Optional[A], E]]`, and
`ResultT[OptionalT[M], E]` carries `M[Optional[Result[A, E]]]`. Either an
absence or a stored error skips later callbacks and lazy right operands,
without converting one failure kind into the other. Native exceptions from any
stage propagate with their exact types instead of becoming `Result` data.

Traversal into a layer delegates to the base's traversal loop with the layer's
accumulation rule, so the count of pulls and callback calls is the same over
eager, deferred and third-party bases. A deferred computation can be copied or
replayed only when its stored inputs and callbacks support it; copying an owner
does not make a consuming callback reusable.

Resource owns native scopes; IOResource composes effectful acquisition, use
and outcome-aware release through the same lifecycle. IO uses the existing
Reader, Result and Optional families for typed outcomes and cooperative
cancellation. Ref, Deferred, Semaphore and Queue construct IO recipes over
shared state. The optional Fiber backend requires explicit unsafe_start and
its documented thread-safety obligations.
effects.summary: Reader, State and Writer computations and the OptionalT and ResultT layers, over any base Monad.

effects.async_runtime.description:
This opt-in preview targets the pinned Mojo 1.2 Linux x86-64 toolchain. An
`IO[T, E]` describes asynchronous work producing T or failing with the exact
domain error E; it runs once, when a host drives it. Methods and Pipeline
compose IO values, and `Async[E]` is their family for tail_rec_m, traversal and
attempt. Long sequences run iteratively in constant native stack. Callbacks
stored in an IO must own their state. Native callbacks run on the host thread
and must return cooperatively. No detached work or GPU backend is provided.

Use protocols for custom leaf machines, lifted with IO.lift. Driver owns entered
roots linearly: request cancellation, continue polling, then finish. Checked
Duration and opaque Instant keep deadline arithmetic wide. Only reviewed names
and documented metadata are supported, not private layout or ABI.
effects.async_runtime.summary: Pure-Mojo async IO with Cats Effect vocabulary and structured cooperative execution.

effects.async_runtime.protocols.description:
IO.lift runs a custom Machine as one step of an IO. Each poll returns promptly
with Step.ready or Step.pending. A terminal step
certifies that entered work and cleanup finished or transferred ownership into
the result. Fresh scoped loans end with each poll. External work retains its own
access rights and must drain before release; readiness alone is not memory
synchronization. Public Context is the canonical IOContext, including its clock.
effects.async_runtime.protocols.summary: Extension contracts for cooperative leaves and scoped asynchronous bodies.

functions.description:
Start with `pipeline(value)`, chain payload operations such as `.map(function)`
or whole-value stages with `.then(function)`, and finish with `.get()`. Native
containers and declared effect recipes infer their family. Select another
family once with `pipeline[Family](value)` and select native callback errors
with `.raising[ErrorType]()`. Plain functions, closures and library callables
can be passed directly to these operations.

Use `pipe(value, f, g)` to apply a fixed sequence now, or `flow(f, g)` and
`compose(g, f)` to build a reusable composition. `flip` swaps two arguments;
`partial` binds leading arguments. `tupled(function)` adapts a binary callback
to one native pair without copying either element, while `untupled(function)`
adapts a pair consumer to two arguments. `first[Other]`, `second[Other]` and
`split(left, right)` transform pair elements; `merge(left, right)` computes
two results from one copyable input.

Two-stage `flow` and `compose` can mix a plain function or stored thin pointer
with a library callable directly, in either position. Compositions own their
stages and preserve their shared, mutable or consuming receiver capabilities.
Inferred two-stage `pipe` also accepts a native/library pair, borrowing its
shared library stage for immediate execution. Extend a saved composition with
`.then(next)` or adapt its input with `.compose(before)`.

`Pipeline.map` follows the selected family's payload and timing rules. Native
collections are eager; Reader, State and Writer retain their base's deferred
execution. `.get()` extracts the carrier; `.run(...)` executes or unwraps a
selected effect. Use `iterated` for lazy collection stages. Native callback
borrows retained by a deferred computation must outlive it.

`as_unary` and `as_binary` provide callable values when a native function must
be stored, such as inside an effect passed to `ap`. Existing `piped(value)`
and its per-method family selections remain compatibility entry points; their
signatures and native-error inference follow the compatibility guide.

`kleisli[Family](f).then(g)` composes effectful functions through the family's
monadic bind. Its `map` transforms successful payloads; ordinary container
`map(chain)` borrows the chain automatically, including in lazy iterators.
functions.summary: Pipelines, compositions, argument flipping and partial application.

iteration.description:
Every operation consumes a **source**: a native iterator, used as it is and
never restarted, or an owned collection (any `IterableOwned`, such as `List`,
`Set` or `Dict`), consumed as `iter(values^)` would. Pass `values^` to consume
a collection, or `iter(values)` to borrow it. Standard adapters (`chain`, `zip`,
`enumerate`, `take`, `drop`, `peekable`, ...) come from `std.iter` and
`std.itertools` and combine freely with these.

`iterated(source)` adds consuming method syntax to the same native iterators:
`iterated(values^).map(f).filter(p).to_list()`. Its `Iter` wrapper implements
`Iterator` and `IterableOwned`, so standard consuming adapters accept it
directly. Native `take`, `drop`, `enumerate`, variadic `zip` and `chain` are
also consuming methods. Wrap another standard adapter's result with `iterated`
to continue chaining.
`to_list()` and `collect_list()` are alias methods for the free `collect_list`.
Named chains are consumed explicitly, as in `stream^.to_list()`.
The core functions `map`, `filter`, `filter_not` and `fold_left` are also exported by
`fp.combinators`; both imports refer to the same native functions. `Piped` adds
the same named methods to eager value chains. Its fold keeps the accumulator
inside the chain, while `Iter.fold_left` returns the accumulator directly.

**Lazy adapters** (`map`, `filter`, `filter_not`, `filter_map`, `flatten`, `flat_map`,
`scan_left`, `zip_with`, `map_with_index` and value-taking `take_while`/`drop_while`)
are native iterators whose advancement raises only
`StopIteration`:

- Construction is inert: nothing is pulled and no callback runs until the first
  `next`.
- They are fused: after a source reports exhaustion it is never pulled again.
- There is no lookahead: each output pulls only what it needs.
- Abandoning one destroys its owned state without evaluating the rest.

Lazy callbacks do not raise, because a native iterator can raise only
`StopIteration`; to carry a domain failure, yield `Result` elements and
aggregate them with `collect_results`. A callback is a plain function, a
capturing closure or a library callable such as a `Partial`. `map`, `filter_map`
and `flat_map` accept shared or mutable unary receivers; `scan_left` accepts
shared or mutable binary callbacks. Move a closure that
owns non-trivial state in with `callback^`. On Mojo 1.1, some native closures
with move-only inputs/output and owned mutable state require `@always_inline`
on the callback to preserve state writes at O3; see the native-boundaries
architecture chapter. Owners of borrowed captures must
stay alive and unmoved while the adapter is used. A generic function that
returns an adapter names its type with `MapIterator`, `ScanIterator`,
`FilterIterator`, `FilterNotIterator`, `FilterMapIterator` or `FlatMapIterator`, declares
`I: Iterator` and `where I.Element == T`, and builds the value through the
function; the types add no storage, and the source origin stays part of the
type.

**Folds and terminals** (`fold_left`, `fold_until`, `reduce`,
`reduce_optional`, `collect_list`, `find`, `any`, `all`) run at once:

| Operation | Non-empty input | Empty input |
|---|---|---|
| `fold_left(step, initial, source)` | `n` calls of `step(var A, var T) -> A`, in order | `initial`, no calls |
| `reduce(step, source, initial=value)` | The same as `fold_left` | `initial`, no calls |
| `reduce(step, source)` | The first element seeds the accumulator; `n - 1` calls | Raises `EmptyReductionError` |
| `reduce_optional(step, source)` | As above, wrapped in `Optional` | `None` |
| `fold_until(step, initial, source)` | Each call returns `ControlFlow[B, A]`; `Break(b)` returns at once | `Continue(initial)` |
| `collect_list(source)` | A `List` of every element, moved | An empty list |
| `first(source)` / `last(source)` | First / last remaining element | `None` |
| `is_empty(source)` | Pulls at most one value; returns `False` | `True` |
| `count(source)` / `count_where(p, source)` | Visits and counts values / matches | `0` |
| `contains(source, value)` | Borrows for equality, stops at first match | `False` |
| `for_each(f, source)` | Moves each value into a callback returning `NoneType` | `None`, no calls |
| `to_non_empty_list(source)` | `Some(NonEmptyList)` | `None` |
| `combine_all_optional[S](source)` | Left-to-right Semigroup reduction | `None` |
| `collect_fold[M](f, source)` | Combines present Optional results with the Monoid | Monoid identity |
| `find(p, source)` | The first accepted element | `None` |
| `any(p, source)` / `all(p, source)` | Stops at the first decisive element | `False` / `True` |

Steps are never reassociated. Pure and raising callbacks have separate
overloads, and a callback's error type propagates unchanged; a callback that
raises `StopIteration` fails as a callback, never as exhaustion. The first
decisive result or failure stops without another pull. On failure, native
cleanup destroys the source, the current accumulator and the pulled element;
side effects are not rolled back. Every operation makes `O(n)` callback calls,
or fewer after an early stop, with constant extra state.

A generic function forwards to these with the native callback constraint and
`where I.Element == T`. A raising wrapper passes `E=E` at every call and must
not read `F.E` or `F.T` from a callback type: Mojo 1.1 does not reliably expose
those attributes through a precompiled package. Keep the parameter names shown
in the tutorial's generic examples; on Mojo 1.1 some renamings lose callback
conformance.
iteration.summary: Lazy adapters, folds, reductions and terminal operations over native iterators.

matching.description:
`match` takes a `Node` value, or two or three values, and one to sixteen
clauses: plain functions or lambdas without captures, whose parameter types
select the constructors they handle. The clauses are checked when the program
compiles and the match runs as one loop, so it is exhaustive, ends on every
value and is not limited by the native stack. `when` adds a guard to a clause,
`Next` continues with a smaller value, and `rewrite` transforms a value
bottom-up. Declare data with `fp.adt.Data`, `Cases` and `Node`.
matching.summary: Pattern matching on algebraic data: `match`, `rewrite`, `when` and `Next`.
